title: The Anatomy of a Good Prompt
problem: New users often type a bare question and get a generic, unhelpful answer — then conclude 'AI isn't very good.' Usually the real issue is the prompt is missing the four things a model needs to give a useful answer: who it should act as, what it should actually do, the background that changes what a good answer looks like, and what shape the answer should come back in.

workflow.step: 1. Name a role, if one helps
workflow.detail: Optional: tell the model what perspective to answer from (e.g. 'a patient teacher', 'a skeptical editor'). Skip this line entirely if no role naturally applies — it isn't required for every prompt.

workflow.step: 2. State the actual task in one sentence
workflow.detail: Say what the output should DO — 'compare', 'explain to a beginner', 'shorten to 100 words' — not just a topic word like 'dogs' or 'taxes'.
Add the background information that changes what a good answer looks like: your situation, your existing knowledge, or constraints the model can't guess on its own.
State the length, structure, and tone you want back. Without this, you'll get whatever length/style the model defaults to, which is often wrong for your purpose.

workflow.step: 5. Treat the first answer as a draft
workflow.detail: If it's not quite right, don't retype from scratch — reply with what's wrong ('too formal', 'shorter', 'add an example') and let the model revise in place.

variables.name: ROLE
variables.label: Role (optional — delete if not needed)
variables.placeholder: e.g. Act as a patient teacher explaining this to a total beginner.

variables.name: TASK
variables.label: Task
variables.placeholder: e.g. Explain what compound interest is and why it matters

variables.name: CONTEXT
variables.label: Context
variables.placeholder: e.g. I'm 22, just started my first job, have never taken a finance class

variables.name: FORMAT
variables.label: Format
variables.placeholder: e.g. Under 150 words, plain language, one concrete number example

exampleOutput:
**Bare prompt:** "What is compound interest?" → a generic, textbook-style paragraph.

**Structured prompt (this recipe):** "Act as a patient teacher... I'm 22, just started my first job, have never taken a finance class... under 150 words, one concrete number example" → a short, plain-language explanation using a real dollar example tied to a first paycheck — directly usable, no rewriting needed.
tips: Skip the ROLE line if it doesn't naturally apply — it's optional, not a required ingredient.
If the answer isn't right, don't retype the whole prompt — just say what's wrong and let the model revise; this is faster and usually gets closer to what you wanted.
This basic shape (role, task, context, format) works the same way across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and local models — it's the model-agnostic starting point behind every other recipe in this cookbook.
If you're not sure what context matters, try asking the model 'what information would help you answer this better?' before answering — it will often tell you.
